mem.t: He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.

lessons.title: Looking Back on a Year of Grace
lessons.theme: Raising an Ebenezer: thus far the Lord has helped us

v: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”
Praise the LORD, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits,

lessons.still: Open your notes from this year or the photo album on your phone, and browse slowly. Each time you see a sign of grace, pause and say, “Lord, thus far you have helped me.” Don’t rush; let thankfulness well up, layer upon layer.
teach: When climbers reach the summit, they often turn around and look back down the way they came: the steep slope, the sheer drop, the place where they almost gave up. Only by looking back do they see how far they have come, and who helped them along the way. Today we stand on the summit of a year, looking back and counting our blessings.

After defeating the Philistines at Mizpah, Samuel set up a stone and named it Ebenezer, meaning “stone of help.” He said, “until now.” This was not an end point but a marker: God helped in the past, and God will surely help in the future. David too commanded his own soul: “Don’t forget all his benefits!” We find it easiest to remember our failures and easiest to forget God’s grace.

This year we have walked through four stages. Rooting (Weeks 1–13): coming home, stillness, Scripture, prayer, humility. Growing (Weeks 14–26): identity, the self-emptied life, the Holy Spirit, self-denial. Fruiting (Weeks 27–39): 920 and the ninefold fruit of the Spirit. Multiplying (Weeks 40–52): 235 relationships, gifts, unity, the kingdom. Each stage is an Ebenezer that God has set up with his own hands.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Changing our mindset changes our life, and changing our life changes our way of living. Looking back over the year is Review carried out in grace: not counting up our own performance, but counting up what God has done. Everything is grace that God has accomplished in Jesus, and the glory goes to him.
q: Who is God? — Looking back over this year, at what moments did God especially show himself as “the God who helps you”?
Who am I? — Of the four stages, in which did you change the most?
How shall I respond? — How will you set up an “Ebenezer” for this year?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus instituted the Lord’s Supper, he said, “Do this in memory of me.” He knew how easily we forget, so he gave us a way to remember. Looking back on grace is remembering the Lord who has walked with us all the way and gave himself for us.
lessons.pray: God who helps me, thus far you have helped me. Thank you for bringing me home this year, and for rooting, growing, fruiting and multiplying in me. My soul, do not forget all his benefits! I offer every step of this year to you; all the glory belongs to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the ten most memorable signs of grace from this year
Choose an object as this year’s “Ebenezer” and put it where you will often see it
Share with a family member or companion one way God helped you this year
lessons.noon: “The LORD helped us until now.” — Lord, right now I remember all your benefits.

lessons.title: The Overcomer’s Promise
lessons.theme: From knocking at the door to sitting on the throne: the overcomer’s path

v: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with me.
He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne, as I also overcame and sat down with my Father on his throne.
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”

lessons.still: Listen quietly, as if you can hear someone knocking at the door. This year the Lord has knocked at your door again and again. Now open the door of your heart and say to him, “Lord, please come in and eat with me.”
teach: A year ago we began with the prodigal son coming home: the father running to embrace the son returning from a distant land. A year later we read the promise of Revelation: the overcomer will sit with the Lord on his throne. From the doorstep to the throne: that is the whole panorama of the gospel. God not only welcomes us home; he wants us to reign with him.

In Revelation 3:20 the Lord stands at the door and knocks, and he is speaking to the lukewarm church in Laodicea. The Lord had not given up on such a church; if anyone opens the door, he will come in and eat with them. The promise of verse 21 is even more astonishing: the overcomer will sit with the Lord on his throne, “as I also overcame.” Our victory does not depend on ourselves; it is a share in Christ’s victory. He says, “I have overcome the world.”

Overcomers are not people who never fall, but people who open the door again and again to let the Lord in. This year you may have had lukewarm seasons, failures and setbacks, but the Lord is still knocking. The secret of overcoming never changes: let Jesus reign. It is not that I have overcome, but that he overcomes in me.
lessons.light: 321 Light: When the old self’s self-ruled life becomes the new self’s self-emptied life, a defeated life becomes an overcoming life. Humility overcomes pride; the self-emptied life overcomes Satan. The overcomer’s crown is not our own achievement; it is to be laid before the throne, so that Jesus receives all the glory.
q: Who is God? — What kind of Lord knocks at the door and also invites you to sit with him on his throne?
Who am I? — Where this year have you experienced “he overcomes in me”?
How shall I respond? — Which door of your heart still needs to be opened today to let the Lord in?
lessons.jesus: On earth Jesus went through temptation, misunderstanding, betrayal and the cross, and then he said, “I have overcome the world.” His victory was not escaping suffering but passing through it. Having overcome, he sat down on his Father’s throne, and now he invites us to overcome with him.
lessons.pray: Victorious Lord Jesus, thank you for knocking at my door again and again this year. Once more I open the door of my heart and invite you in to reign. I do not overcome by my own strength; I overcome as you overcome in me. One day I will lay my crown at your feet, for you are worthy of all glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down one specific experience this year of overcoming through the Lord
Share with someone who is struggling: “The Lord has overcome the world.”
lessons.noon: “He who overcomes, I will give to him to sit down with me on my throne” — Lord, right now I open the door and let you reign.

lessons.title: Sent Out: Becoming Spiritual Parents
lessons.theme: Those who have received grace are sent out to multiply life through life

v: But we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
Even so, affectionately longing for you, we were well pleased to impart to you not the Good News of God only, but also our own souls, because you had become very dear to us.
Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

lessons.still: First call to mind those who led you to faith and walked with you as you grew, and thank God for them. Then think of one or two people around you who are young in faith, and quietly place their names before the Lord: “Lord, I am willing to walk with them.”
teach: A tree bears fruit, the fruit holds seeds, and the seeds fall to the ground and grow into new trees. The final proof of life is not how tall it grows but whether it can bring forth new life. This year we have been rooted, have grown and have borne fruit in the Lord; now the Lord is sending us out so that life may carry on in others.

Paul told the Thessalonians that he was like a nursing mother caring for her own children, sharing with them not only the gospel but “our own souls.” Elsewhere he says, “Though you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, you don’t have many fathers” (1 Corinthians 4:15). Spiritual parents are not speakers on a platform; they are people who walk alongside others, life to life. The risen Lord says, “As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

Becoming a spiritual parent does not require perfection, only being a few steps further along and being willing to walk alongside. From among your “2,” ask the Lord to show you one or two spiritual children: meet regularly, read the Bible and pray together, share life, walk with them without controlling them. Today you are being sent out, carrying this year’s practices with you, to become a spiritual parent in someone else’s life.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The “3” in 235 means having spiritual parents and becoming one. The final step of the eight steps for changing our mindset is Multiplication. Life first, then relationships, then ministry: not designing a training programme first, but first sharing our life with people. This is the grain of wheat falling into the ground and bearing much fruit.
q: Who is God? — “Even so I send you.” What does this show you about how the Lord sees you?
Who am I? — Do you feel you are “not good enough yet” to be someone’s spiritual parent?
How shall I respond? — For which one or two spiritual children will you pray, and arrange to meet this week?
lessons.jesus: Jesus kept twelve ordinary men close to him, eating with them, walking with them and working with them. What he gave them was not just a curriculum but his own life. In the end he sent them out, and they in turn brought forth generation after generation of spiritual children, all the way down to us today.
lessons.pray: Lord who sends me, thank you for raising me up through many spiritual parents. Now I am willing to be sent by you, to share with others what I have received. Show me the people I should walk alongside, and give me a parent’s heart, like a mother nursing her children, willing to share even my own life with them. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the names of one or two spiritual children you are willing to walk with
This week, take the initiative to meet or call one of them
Thank your spiritual parent, and tell them about your desire to be sent out
lessons.noon: “As the Father has sent me, even so I send you” — Lord, right now I am willing to be sent by you.

lessons.title: Stage Self-Review: Examining the Year
lessons.theme: Examining ourselves under God’s searching gaze, hoping in God’s completing work

v: Search me, God, and know my heart. Try me, and know my thoughts.
See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way.
being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

lessons.still: Quietly say, “Search me, God.” Don’t rush to defend yourself, and don’t rush to condemn yourself. Like a patient sitting before a doctor they trust, openly let him examine you, believing it is for your healing.
teach: A health check-up is not meant to frighten us but to catch things early and adjust early. Someone who never has a check-up may seem fine but could be carrying hidden dangers; those who are checked regularly can grow healthier under a doctor’s guidance. The spiritual health self-review is just such an annual check-up.

David asks God, “Search me … try me,” and then asks him to “lead me in the everlasting way.” The goal of self-examination is not to dwell on our faults but to walk the right path. Paul too is confident that he who began a good work in us will complete it. The foundation of self-review is not my performance but God’s faithfulness; not how much I have achieved, but how much more God will complete.

Today, please complete the spiritual health self-review for the fourth stage, and compare it with your results from the first, second and third stages to see the trajectory of the whole year. Which areas have changed? Where does the Lord still need to keep working? Be honest before God, and be hopeful before God. After Review comes Correction, and after Correction comes Repetition: the practice does not end today; it enters a new cycle.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The eight steps for changing our mindset are Information, Revelation, Conviction, Practice, Review, Correction, Repetition and Multiplication. Self-review is the Review step, but we review in grace: our focus is on Jesus, not on our own success or failure. We examine ourselves to respond more deeply to grace, not to earn it.
q: Who is God? — “Will complete it.” How does this help you face your shortcomings?
Who am I? — Comparing your self-reviews across the four stages, what trajectory of growth do you see?
How shall I respond? — In the new year, in which area do you most want to ask the Lord to keep working?
lessons.jesus: The risen Jesus asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” It was a gentle examination, not to shame him but to restore him. After that examination Jesus said, “Feed my sheep.” The Lord’s searching always comes with a new commission.
lessons.pray: Search me, God, and know my heart; try me, and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the everlasting way. Thank you that he who began a good work in me will complete it. I entrust this year to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Complete this stage's spiritual health self-review
Compare your self-reviews across the four stages, and write down three areas of growth and one need
Share what you discovered in your self-review with a spiritual companion or spiritual parent
lessons.noon: “Search me, God, and know my heart” — Lord, right now I stand open before you.

lessons.title: Let Jesus Reign in the New Year
lessons.theme: Heading toward the great revival of the last days, letting Jesus reign in the new year

v: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.
that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

lessons.still: Stand up, open your hands, and offer the new year to the Lord, saying, “Lord Jesus, in the new year you are King.” Then wait quietly, asking the Holy Spirit to pour out on you and on those you love.
teach: One spark lights a torch; one torch lights ten; ten light a hundred. A city at night is not lit by one huge lamp but by thousands upon thousands of small lights shining together. The great revival of the last days likewise begins with lives that are set alight, one by one, and go on to set others alight.

Joel prophesied, “I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.” On the day of Pentecost, Peter declared that this prophecy had begun to be fulfilled. From that day on, the outpouring of the Spirit has spread from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth, and will do so until the Lord returns. Philippians pictures the end: everything in heaven, on earth and under the earth will bow the knee at the name of Jesus, and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. That is where revival is ultimately heading.

This year began with the prodigal coming home and ends today with being sent out. Humility is the key to revival: revival does not begin with large gatherings but with one heart willing to let Jesus reign. In the new year, may the Lord make you a lamp that has been set alight, carrying your 235 relationships into your family, workplace, church and society, building God’s kingdom system and welcoming the Lord’s return.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Three foundations, two cores, one purpose. Jesus is my example; Scripture is my standard; the Holy Spirit is my guide. Let Jesus reign; let Jesus receive all the glory. Build what belongs to God. In the new year, let 321 become the rhythm of your life, until every tongue confesses that Jesus is Lord.
q: Who is God? — What is the heart of the God who promises to pour out his Spirit on all flesh toward the last generation?
Who am I? — Are you willing to be a torch in the revival of the last days?
How shall I respond? — In the new year, in what concrete way will you let Jesus reign every day?
lessons.jesus: Before his ascension Jesus promised, “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you.” He ascended to the Father’s right hand, poured out the Spirit, and is still extending his kingdom today. He is both the source and the goal of revival: every knee will bow to him.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, in the new year I give the throne to you. Pour out your Spirit on me, my family, my church and my city, and make me a lamp that is set alight and that sets others alight. May every knee bow to you and every tongue confess that you are Lord. Come, Lord Jesus! In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a “Let Jesus Reign” declaration for the new year, then sign and date it
Pray with one heart with a fellow soldier for the great revival of the last days
Plan your quiet times and your times of walking with others for the first week of the new year
lessons.noon: “I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh” — Lord, right now set me alight; in the new year you are King.
